title: Learning target family size bound
statement: Let $n$ be a natural number, let $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\{\pm1\}$, let $t\in\mathbb Q$ be positive, and let $\varepsilon\in\mathbb Q$ satisfy $0<\varepsilon\leq 1/2$. If the total influence of the real-valued version of $f$ is at most $t$, then the learning-consequences target family determined by $f,t,\varepsilon$ has cardinality at most the learning-consequences family bound determined by $t,\varepsilon$.
hypotheses_covered: $f$ is a sign-valued function on the Boolean cube of dimension $n$
the total influence of the real-valued version of $f$ is at most $t$
caveat: The target family and its bound are referenced only through upstream definitions whose informal descriptions are placeholders, so their full mathematical meaning cannot be stated here without expanding those definitions.
